mainTopic: The guarantor (עָרֵב): when a lender may collect from him, why he is obligated at all, and how he differs from a קבלן.
overview: The משנה finishes its rules about a guarantor (עָרֵב). If the lender set a condition to collect 'from whomever I wish,' he may collect from the עָרֵב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if the borrower has property, he may not. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also rules that a husband divorcing a wife whose כתובה has a guarantor must vow off benefit from her, so the couple cannot plot against the guarantor. The גמרא first explains the משנה through רבה and רב יוסף: the guarantor only answers for producing the borrower. רב נחמן rejects this as unreasonable, 'like a Persian court,' and explains that the lender simply may not go to the עָרֵב first. A ברייתא supports him. The גמרא then looks for a פסוק showing that a עָרֵב is obligated. It rejects the story of יהודה and בנימין as קבלנות and accepts פסוקים from משלי. אמימר ties the guarantor's obligation to the dispute over אסמכתא. רב אשי rejects this and explains that the עָרֵב truly commits because he enjoys being trusted. Finally, רבי יוחנן limits the 'whomever I wish' condition to a borrower with no property. The גמרא explains that the משנה is missing words and contrasts a regular עָרֵב with a קבלן.

steps.title: A condition lets the lender collect from the guarantor
steps.stepSummary: If the lender stated the condition 'I will collect from whomever I wish,' he may collect directly from the עָרֵב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the lender said to the borrower, 'I lend on condition that I can collect from whoever I want,' then he may collect from the guarantor.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exception to its earlier rule that a lender cannot go straight to the guarantor. A clear condition lets him do so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said the lender may not collect from the עָרֵב. Here, because the lender openly set terms letting him pick whom to collect from, the guarantor agreed to be collected from directly. The condition changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: guarantor, the person who backs a loan

phrases.english: But if he said to him:
phrases.notes: The lender is the one speaking, and he is talking to the borrower.

phrases.english: "On condition that I will collect from whomever I wish"
phrases.notes: He means either the borrower or the guarantor, whichever one he chooses.

phrases.english: he may collect from the guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶפָּרַע מִמִּי שֶׁאֶרְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier part of the משנה, which said a lender may not collect from the guarantor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the condition 'from whomever I wish,' the lender may collect directly from the עָרֵב.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל protects the guarantor when the borrower has property
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if the borrower has property, the lender cannot collect from the עָרֵב, with or without a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if the borrower has property, then either way, with the condition or without it, the lender may not collect from the guarantor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion. In his view, the borrower's own property always comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said the condition allows collecting from the עָרֵב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the condition does not help as long as the borrower has assets. The lender must collect from the borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: either way, in this case or that case

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If the borrower has property,
whether this way or that way,
phrases.notes: Whether or not the lender made the condition from the line before.

phrases.english: he may not collect from the guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אִם יֵשׁ נְכָסִים לַלֹּוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the borrower has assets, the lender never collects from the עָרֵב, even with a condition.
steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion says a condition lets the lender go to the guarantor. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the borrower's own property always comes first.

steps.title: A guarantor for a כתובה: the husband must vow off his wife
steps.stepSummary: When someone guarantees a wife's כתובה and the husband divorces her, he must take a vow to get no benefit from her, so the couple cannot plot to take the guarantor's money and then remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also used to say: if someone is a guarantor for a woman's כתובה, and her husband was divorcing her, the husband must vow to get no benefit from her. Otherwise they might plot against this guarantor's property, and then he would take his wife back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a second rule that also protects a guarantor. This time the case is a guarantor for a כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A couple could fake a divorce so the wife collects her כתובה from the guarantor, and then remarry. Requiring the husband to vow off all benefit from her makes remarriage impossible, so the plot would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: marriage contract, which promises the wife money on divorce or the husband's death
he must vow to get no benefit from her
a scheme, a plot made together

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And so Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say:
A guarantor for a woman for her marriage contract,
and her husband was divorcing her,
he must make a vow forbidding benefit from her,
lest they make a scheme
against the property of this one,
and he will take back his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The word וְכֵן links this to step 2 as another ruling by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that protects the guarantor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband divorcing a wife whose כתובה has a guarantor must vow off benefit from her, to prevent a plot against the guarantor.
steps.whatToRemember: Both rulings of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל protect the guarantor from being taken advantage of.

steps.title: The גמרא asks why the guarantor is protected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's rule that the lender cannot collect from the guarantor.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the lender cannot go to the guarantor. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question points back to the earlier rule in the משנה, that one who lends with a guarantor may not collect from him. At this point the גמרא understands the guarantor as responsible only in limited situations, and it wants the logic behind that.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: This asks about the earlier line in the משנה: a lender with a guarantor may not collect from the guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא's analysis of its basic rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the lender may not collect from the עָרֵב.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: 'You gave me a man, I give you back a man'
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain that the guarantor only took responsibility for the borrower as a person. Since the borrower is right here, the guarantor hands him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: the guarantor tells the lender, 'You handed a man over to me; I am handing the man back to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. In their view the guarantor's job was only to make sure the borrower is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this reading, the guarantor only answers for the borrower disappearing. If the borrower is present, the guarantor says, 'Here he is, go collect from him.' He has no further duty, even if the borrower cannot pay.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
"You gave a man over to me,"
phrases.notes: The guarantor is talking to the lender. The "man" is the borrower.

phrases.english: "I have given a man back to you."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The guarantor only took responsibility for producing the borrower. If the borrower is present, the guarantor owes nothing.

steps.title: רב נחמן: that is Persian law
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that the reasoning of רבה and רב יוסף matches Persian law, not Jewish law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objects: this is the law of the Persians!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the answer of רבה and רב יוסף. He says it describes a foreign legal system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן says that a guarantor who only answers for the borrower as a person is how Persian law works. In his view, that cannot be the meaning of a Jewish guarantor's duty. The explanation in step 5 is now under challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman objects to this:
This is Persian law!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רבה and רב יוסף that the guarantor only answers for producing the borrower.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a limited guarantee is the rule of Persian law. Jewish law should not be explained that way.

steps.title: Persian courts actually go after the guarantor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's remark. Persian courts go straight after the עָרֵב, which is the opposite of what רבה and רב יוסף said.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, the Persian courts go after the guarantor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב נחמן's comparison. Persian courts do the reverse of what רבה and רב יוסף said, because they collect from the guarantor directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רב יוסף let the guarantor off whenever the borrower is around. רב נחמן called that 'Persian law.' But Persian courts are known for chasing the guarantor first, so the comparison seems backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
They go after; they turn to

phrases.english: On the contrary,
they go after the guarantor!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, בָּתַר עָרְבָא אָזְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the comparison רב נחמן made in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the view of רבה and רב יוסף matches Persian law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Persian courts collect from the guarantor first, which is the opposite of letting him off. So the label 'Persian law' does not fit.

steps.title: He meant it is an arbitrary ruling, like a Persian court's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב נחמן did not mean Persian courts hold this rule. He meant that letting the עָרֵב off is the kind of ruling Persian judges make, with no reason behind it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant it fits a Persian court, which gives no reason for its rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the misunderstanding of what רב נחמן meant by 'Persian.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison is not about the content of Persian law. It is about how unreasonable the ruling is. Freeing the עָרֵב hurts the lender, who relied on him, and there is no good reason for that.

phrases.english: Rather, he meant a Persian court –
phrases.notes: He means the ruling is the kind of thing a Persian court would decide, not that Persian law actually says this.

phrases.english: which does not give a reason for its words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּי דִינָא דְפָרְסָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן meant that Persian law actually frees the guarantor.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן meant that freeing the guarantor is arbitrary, like the unreasoned rulings of Persian judges.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reading: the lender cannot go to the guarantor first
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains the משנה differently. 'He cannot collect from the עָרֵב' only means the lender cannot claim from the עָרֵב first. He must try the borrower before turning to the עָרֵב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: What does 'he cannot collect from the guarantor' mean? It means he cannot claim from the guarantor first.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the explanation of רבה and רב יוסף, רב נחמן gives his own answer to what the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רב יוסף read the משנה as freeing the עָרֵב completely. רב נחמן reads it as a rule about order: borrower first, then עָרֵב. The עָרֵב is still responsible if the borrower does not pay.

keyTerms.meaning: He cannot collect (the words of the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן does NOT say the guarantor is free. He only says the lender has to go to the borrower first. If the borrower cannot pay, the guarantor must pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the working understanding of a regular guarantor. He is a backup who pays only after the borrower fails.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Naḥman said:
What is 'he cannot collect from the guarantor'?
He cannot claim from the guarantor first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מַאי לֹא יִפָּרַע מִן הֶעָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation of רבה and רב יוסף from step 5 with a new reading of the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה only means the lender cannot demand payment from the guarantor before first trying the borrower.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן. The lender may not claim from the עָרֵב first. But if he made the condition 'I will collect from whomever I want,' he may go to the עָרֵב first.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too a ברייתא teaches: One who lends with a guarantor cannot claim from the guarantor first. But if he said 'on condition that I collect from whomever I want,' he can claim from the guarantor first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the exact words of רב נחמן, as support for his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'לא יתבע ערב תחלה', the same phrase רב נחמן used. That shows the issue is only which one to claim from first. The stipulation case fits too: with that condition, the lender may skip the borrower and go straight to the עָרֵב.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (a support)

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, a regular עָרֵב pays only after the borrower is tried first. If the lender stipulated 'from whomever I want,' he may go to the עָרֵב first.

phrases.english: It is also taught so (in a baraita):

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל יְדֵי עָרֵב –
phrases.english: One who lends to his fellow through a guarantor –
cannot claim from the guarantor first.
But if he said:
'On condition that I collect from whomever I want' –
he can claim from the guarantor first.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's reading from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's reading that the משנה is about the order of collection, not about freeing the guarantor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says in the same words: 'לא יתבע ערב תחלה', with the stipulation exception.

steps.title: רב הונא's source: יהודה guarantees בנימין
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks where we learn that a עָרֵב is obligated. He answers from יהודה's words to יעקב: 'I will be his guarantor; from my hand shall you request him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Where do we learn that a guarantor becomes obligated? From the פסוק 'I will be his guarantor; from my hand shall you request him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It wants a source that a עָרֵב is legally bound to pay, and רב הונא offers one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A עָרֵב never received the money himself, so we need a reason why his words alone obligate him. רב הונא points to יהודה, who made himself responsible for בנימין. That shows a person can take responsibility for something that belongs to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall request him or demand him

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
From where do we know that a guarantor becomes obligated?
As it is written:
"I will be his guarantor;
from my hand shall you request him."
phrases.notes: בראשית 43:9. This is יהודה promising יעקב that he will bring בנימין back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מִנַּיִן לְעָרֵב דְּמִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of whom the lender collects from first to the basic question of why a עָרֵב is obligated at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A עָרֵב is obligated, and the source is יהודה's guarantee for בנימין.

steps.title: רב חסדא: That was full responsibility, not a regular guarantee
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects that יהודה's case was קבלנות, full unconditional responsibility, as shown by a parallel פסוק with ראובן: 'Give him into my hand and I will bring him back.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא challenged this: But that is a case of קבלנות, as it is written, 'Give him into my hand, and I will bring him back to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רב הונא's source. He says the בנימין story is not about an ordinary עָרֵב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קַבְּלָן takes the whole obligation on himself, almost like a borrower. A regular עָרֵב only backs up the borrower. Since בנימין was handed over into the brothers' own hands, the story proves the law of a קַבְּלָן, not the law of a regular עָרֵב.

keyTerms.meaning: Full, unconditional responsibility (stronger than a regular guarantee)

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying a עָרֵב is not obligated. He only says this פסוק is about a different, stronger kind of guarantee, so it cannot be the source.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda objects to it:
But this is an unconditional guarantee!
As it is written:
"Give him into my hand,
and I will bring him back!"
phrases.notes: בראשית 42:37. These are ראובן's words about בנימין.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא קַבְּלָנוּת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the פסוק רב הונא brought in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's proof from יהודה and בנימין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בנימין case was קבלנות, as shown by the parallel פסוק, so it does not teach the law of an ordinary עָרֵב.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's source from משלי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings a new source from משלי: 'Take his garment, because he was a guarantor for a stranger.' The lender may take the עָרֵב's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יצחק said the source is from here: 'Take his garment, because he was a guarantor for a stranger, and hold him as a pledge for a foreign woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב הונא's source was rejected, רבי יצחק replaces it with a פסוק that clearly talks about an ordinary guarantor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the lender to take the garment of the one who guaranteed someone else's debt. That shows the עָרֵב's own property can be taken for the loan, so he is truly obligated.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yitzchak said,
from here:
"Take his garment, because he was a guarantor for a stranger,
and for a foreign woman, hold him as a pledge."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new source after רב חסדא rejected רב הונא's source.
steps.raayaObject: That a regular עָרֵב is obligated to pay
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 20:16, 'Take his garment, because he was a guarantor for a stranger'

steps.title: A second verse: the guarantor is trapped by his words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds משלי 6:1-3, which says a guarantor is caught by his own words, and explains 'התרפס' as 'open your hand' if you owe money, or 'gather friends' to ask forgiveness if you do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also says: 'My son, if you became a guarantor for your friend and shook hands for a stranger, you are trapped and caught by the words of your mouth. Do this, my son, and save yourself, since you came into your friend's hand: go, humble yourself, and gather your friends.' If you hold his money, open your hand and pay him. If not, bring many friends to ask him to forgive you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק to support רבי יצחק, and then explains the end of that פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a guarantor is 'caught by the words of his mouth', so his words alone bind him. The גמרא reads 'הִתְרַפֵּס' as two words, הַתֵּר פִּיסַּת, 'open the palm': if you owe money, pay it. If you only hurt him with words, gather friends to help you ask forgiveness.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says (a second פסוק is added)
You shook hands, meaning you made a binding promise
Humble yourself; the גמרא reads it as הַתֵּר פִּיסַּת, 'open the palm'

steps.whatToRemember: A עָרֵב is obligated because of his words. רב הונא's source from בנימין was rejected as קבלנות, and the accepted sources are the פסוקים in משלי.

phrases.english: And it says:
"My son, if you became a guarantor for your friend,
if you shook hands for a stranger,
you are trapped by the words of your mouth,
you are caught by the words of your mouth.
Do this then, my son, and save yourself,
since you have come into your friend's hand:
go, humble yourself, and gather your friends."
If he has money in your hand,
open up the palm of your hand for him;
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא reads הִתְרַפֵּס: as הַתֵּר פִּיסַּת, meaning open your hand and pay.

phrases.english: and if not,
gather many friends to him.
phrases.notes: If you don't owe him money but hurt him with words, bring friends along to help you ask him to forgive you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: בְּנִי, אִם עָרַבְתָּ לְרֵעֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק from משלי to back up רבי יצחק's source, and explains its ending.
steps.raayaObject: That a guarantor is bound by his words and must pay
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 6:1-3, 'if you became a guarantor for your friend, you are trapped by the words of your mouth'

steps.title: אמימר ties the guarantor's obligation to the אסמכתא dispute
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says that whether a עָרֵב is bound depends on the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי over אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: Whether a עָרֵב becomes obligated is a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. According to רבי יוסי, who says an אסמכתא works, a עָרֵב is obligated. According to רבי יהודה, who says an אסמכתא does not work, a עָרֵב is not obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר asks why a עָרֵב is really bound. He says the answer depends on a known argument about אסמכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A עָרֵב promises to pay only if the borrower fails to pay, and he expects that will never happen. That looks like an אסמכתא, a promise made without full commitment. So אמימר says the עָרֵב is bound only for the side that holds an אסמכתא works, which is רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: A conditional promise made without real commitment, because the person expects the condition will never happen
It works: it creates a binding obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. רבי יוסי says אסמכתא DOES work, so for him the עָרֵב is bound. רבי יהודה says it does NOT work, so for him the עָרֵב is not bound.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
whether a guarantor becomes obligated
is a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei;
according to Rabbi Yosei, who says:
an asmakhta works,
phrases.notes: The guarantor only pays if the borrower fails to pay, which he doesn't expect. That's what makes it look like an אסמכתא.

phrases.english: a guarantor is obligated.
According to Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
an asmakhta does not work,
a guarantor is not obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: עָרֵב דְּמִשְׁתַּעְבַּד, מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier steps found פסוקים showing that a עָרֵב is bound. Now אמימר asks about the logic: how can such a conditional promise bind at all?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether a עָרֵב is bound depends on the אסמכתא dispute. For רבי יוסי he is bound, and for רבי יהודה he is not.

steps.title: רב אשי objects from everyday practice
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that in daily practice we hold that אסמכתא does not work, yet a עָרֵב is still bound. So the two issues cannot depend on each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But we see every day that an אסמכתא does not work, and still a עָרֵב is obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר's link. Everyday practice holds both rules at once: אסמכתא does not work, and a עָרֵב is still bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אמימר were right, then the accepted rule that אסמכתא does not work would mean a עָרֵב is never bound. But everyone accepts that a עָרֵב IS bound. So the עָרֵב's obligation must come from some other reason.

keyTerms.meaning: An everyday occurrence: something accepted and done in practice all the time

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But these are everyday occurrences,
that an asmakhta does not work
and yet a guarantor is obligated!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: הָא מַעֲשִׂים בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks אמימר's claim that the עָרֵב's obligation depends on the אסמכתא dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's link between the עָרֵב's obligation and the rule of אסמכתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Accepted practice holds that אסמכתא does not work AND that a עָרֵב is bound. So the second cannot depend on the first.

steps.title: רב אשי: the guarantor commits because he enjoys being trusted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the עָרֵב fully commits himself because of the satisfaction he gets from being trusted. That is why his promise is not a weak אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Because of the satisfaction he gets from being trusted, the עָרֵב makes up his mind and truly obligates himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own reason why a עָרֵב is bound. He is bound even though אסמכתא normally does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא fails because the person never really meant to commit. A עָרֵב is different. The lender gives the loan because he trusts the עָרֵב, and the עָרֵב enjoys that trust. In return he truly commits. So this case does not belong to the אסמכתא question at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He fully made up his mind

steps.whatToRemember: A עָרֵב is bound even though אסמכתא does not work. The reason is that being trusted gives him satisfaction, and that makes his commitment real.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the accepted reason why a guarantor is bound in הלכה. It also shows that a conditional promise can bind when the person gets some benefit that makes him truly commit.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
through that satisfaction
of being trusted by him,
phrases.notes: The lender trusts the guarantor and hands over the money because of him.

phrases.english: he makes up his mind and obligates himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּהָהוּא הֲנָאָה דְּקָא מְהֵימַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אמימר's approach, רב אשי offers a new reason for the עָרֵב's obligation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier explanation with a new reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עָרֵב's promise is an אסמכתא, so it depends on the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The satisfaction of being trusted makes the עָרֵב fully commit. So he is bound even according to the view that אסמכתא does not work.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the 'collect from whomever I want' condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's condition. רבי יוחנן says the lender may go to the עָרֵב first only when the borrower has no property. If the borrower has property, the lender may not collect from the עָרֵב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if he said, on condition that I collect from whomever I want...' רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only when the borrower has no property. But if the borrower has property, the lender may not collect from the עָרֵב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and brings רבי יוחנן's limit on it. The condition lets the lender go to the עָרֵב first only if the borrower has nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the condition, the lender must first try the borrower. רבי יוחנן says the condition only saves the lender from first having to sue a borrower who has no property. It does not let him skip a borrower who does have property.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when: a phrase that limits the case of the משנה
Etc.: the quote from the משנה continues

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the condition lets the lender go to the עָרֵב whenever he likes. According to רבי יוחנן, it only helps when the borrower has no property.

phrases.english: And if he said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here. 'He' is the lender, speaking when he gives the loan.

phrases.english: 'on condition that I collect from whomever I want,' etc.
Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this only
when the borrower has no property,
but if the borrower has property,
he may not collect from the guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶפָּרַע מִמִּי שֶׁאֶרְצֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of why a עָרֵב is bound. It goes back to the משנה's line about the condition 'from whomever I wish' (step 1), which the ברייתא in step 10 also mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The condition 'I will collect from whomever I want' lets the lender go to the עָרֵב first only when the borrower has no property. If the borrower has property, he may not collect from the עָרֵב.

steps.title: Challenge from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Since רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a lender cannot collect from the עָרֵב when the borrower has property, it seems the תנא קמא holds there is no such limit. That contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look: the end of the משנה quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying that if the borrower has property, the lender may not collect from the guarantor. That implies the first תנא holds it makes no difference either way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's rule from step 18 by pointing to the next line in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the 'collect from whomever I wish' condition works only when the borrower has no property. But the משנה puts that limit in the mouth of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which suggests it is his own opinion. If so, the תנא קמא lets the lender go to the עָרֵב whether or not the borrower has property, and רבי יוחנן's reading of the תנא קמא looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part or end of a משנה
By implication, from what it suggests
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If the borrower has property,
he may not collect from the guarantor,
by implication, the first tanna holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא הָכִי וְלָא שְׁנָא הָכִי!
phrases.english: it makes no difference this way, and no difference that way!
phrases.notes: He means: whether or not the borrower has property, the lender can still go to the guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement in step 18 using the end of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the תנא קמא lets the lender go to the עָרֵב only when the borrower has no property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the משנה gives the 'borrower has property' limit as the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the תנא קמא apparently disagrees and has no such limit.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: the full reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה is incomplete and fills it in. A regular עָרֵב pays only if the borrower has no property, even with the special condition. A קבלן pays even if the borrower has property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: If someone lends with a guarantor, he cannot collect from the guarantor first. If he said 'on condition that I may collect from whomever I want,' he may collect from the guarantor. When is that true? When the borrower has no property. But if the borrower has property, he may not collect from the guarantor. An unconditional guarantor, though, can be made to pay even if the borrower has property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the משנה left words out, and then gives the full wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words added, the limit 'only when the borrower has no property' belongs to the main ruling of the משנה, so it matches רבי יוחנן. The new contrast is between a regular עָרֵב and a קבלן: the 'borrower has property' limit applies to the עָרֵב, but not to the קבלן, who can be collected from right away. Since the תנא קמא now holds this limit too, what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees about has to be explained again, and the next amud does that.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words; something must be filled in
In what case is this said? (limits the ruling to a specific case)
An unconditional guarantor, who can be asked to pay directly even if the borrower can pay

steps.whatToRemember: A regular עָרֵב, even with the 'from whomever I want' condition, pays only when the borrower has no property. A קבלן can be made to pay even when the borrower has property.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of guarantor. The 'only if the borrower has no property' limit is about a regular עָרֵב; a קבלן is the exception who can be collected from anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the practical difference between a regular עָרֵב and a קבלן, and confirms רבי יוחנן's rule as the meaning of the משנה.

phrases.english: It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל יְדֵי עָרֵב –
phrases.english: One who lends to his fellow with a guarantor
may not collect from the guarantor.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר ״עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֶפָּרַע מִמִּי שֶׁאֶרְצֶה״ –
phrases.english: But if he said, "On condition that I may collect from whomever I wish,"
he may collect from the guarantor.
In what case is this said?
When the borrower has no property;
phrases.notes: This is just what רבי יוחנן said back in step 18.

phrases.english: but if the borrower has property,
he may not collect from the guarantor.
But an unconditional guarantor,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ נְכָסִים לַלֹּוֶה –
phrases.english: even though the borrower has property,
he may collect from the unconditional guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by restoring missing words in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'borrower has property' limit seemed to be רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own opinion, implying the תנא קמא has no such limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit is part of the main ruling about a regular עָרֵב, matching רבי יוחנן; the contrast in the משנה is with a קבלן, who can be collected from even when the borrower has property.
